## Counterfactuals Are Scientific Scissors {#sec-lay-ch11}

## A Concrete Picture

A baker wants to know what yeast contributed to a loaf. Removing yeast from the
finished loaf is impossible. Baking a second loaf without yeast changes the rise,
temperature history, moisture, and structure. Comparing one instant of the two
doughs answers a different question from comparing the finished loaves.

Models let us make more precise cuts, but each cut has a meaning. We can change
a torque at one frozen state and recompute acceleration. We can continue that
altered branch forward. We can rerun the whole swing with a different schedule,
or change gravity, damping, shaft flexibility, or contact geometry. These are
different experiments, not interchangeable ways to measure one contribution.

![A Copied Complete State Supports Pointwise Input Comparison and Two Forward Futures.](figures/proximal_distal_companion/fig_companion_counterfactual_fork.svg){#fig-lay-counterfactual-fork width=98% fig-alt="Conceptual diagram: one complete state branches into retained-input and changed-input acceleration evaluations, then two separately evolving trajectories. It does not depict changed preparation or mechanism ablation."}

## How the Mechanism Works

Start by naming the question and its observable. Are we asking about an
acceleration at release, clubhead speed after 40 ms, a hand-force peak, or work
up to each branch's own delivery event? Those outcomes need not move together.
Next name what the model permits us to manipulate: a delivered torque, an
actuator command, a controller rule, an internal state, or a model parameter.

A pointwise input intervention holds the complete modeled state fixed and
changes the declared input. Recompute acceleration and reactions under the
same contact mode only if it remains admissible for both inputs. Otherwise
resolve the active mode and declare that change. The difference is the instantaneous consequence
of that intervention within the model. It need not be a unique share of the
observed motion, a derivative, or the consequence of having omitted that input
throughout the preceding swing.

A copied-state forward intervention starts two futures from that same state.
The subsequent difference includes the input change and the geometry, velocity,
contact and feedback changes it causes. Those changes are part of the total
modeled effect; the comparison no longer isolates an instantaneous term.

| Comparison | What Is Held Fixed or Copied? | What Question Does It Answer? |
|---|---|---|
| Pointwise input change | Complete state and declared model mode | How does this input change the current acceleration or reaction? |
| Copied-state forward branch | Complete initial state; declared future policies | What follows over the stated horizon? |
| Changed preparation | Initial conditions and task contract as specified | What trajectory follows from a different whole-swing program? |
| Mechanism ablation | Declared remaining model, with compatible states | Does this specified effect survive this removal? |
| Compensated optimization | Task, admissible controls and constraints | Can another feasible policy recover the selected outcome? |

A human manipulation adds adaptation, feedback and measurement uncertainty.
It tests a biological prediction under an experimental design; it does not
literally implement the model's copied-state intervention.

### Complete State and Physical Input

Copy positions, velocities, flexible modes, activation or transmission states,
controller memory, and any other state needed to determine the next evolution.
For time-dependent dynamics, preserve the time and phase convention too.
Setting an actuator command to zero need not set its delivered torque to zero:
activation, stored elastic energy or a delay can preserve output. Directly
removing delivered torque is a different intervention.

For a declared Markov model, copying all internal state preserves the modeled
influence of prior history. If an omitted history variable changes the future,
the state description is incomplete. A hash helps identify a snapshot, but the
manifest must also state which variables it contains and how they are serialized.

A finite torque step can change acceleration without jumping position or
velocity. It is not an impulse. Contact-mode changes or velocity resets require
their own compatibility, impulse and energy accounting. Merely setting every
velocity to zero can violate a moving constraint and need not describe a
reachable golfer state.

Preload exposes the distinction. A loaded backswing and a different downswing
program may arrive at different transition states; comparing them tests
preparation. Holding geometry and velocity fixed while changing an activation,
gap or elastic state tests an internal-state intervention. Call it that, check
compatibility, and account for any changed stored energy. It cannot also be
called a comparison from identical complete states.

### A Finite Removal Is Not Necessarily an Additive Decomposition

Within a fixed regular mode, an input-affine model has
$\dot x=f_0(x)+G(x)u$. At fixed $x$, changing $u$ to $u'$ gives the exact
baseline-minus-altered vector-field difference $G(x)(u-u')$. This statement requires the named input
coordinates, unchanged model and fixed state. It does not make future
trajectory differences additive, nor guarantee that an upstream actuator
command enters affinely.

A manufactured rotor makes the limitation concrete. Let its inertia be
$I=2\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2}$ and its torque law be
$\tau=k(u_1+u_2)^2$, where $k=3\,\mathrm{N\,m}$ and both commands are
dimensionless. With $u_1=u_2=1$, angular acceleration is
$6\,\mathrm{rad/s^2}$. Removing either command leaves
$1.5\,\mathrm{rad/s^2}$: each separate reduction is
$4.5\,\mathrm{rad/s^2}$. Removing both gives a reduction of
$6$, not $9\,\mathrm{rad/s^2}$. The two removals overlap through the
nonlinear torque law, even before any state has evolved.

Likewise, differentiating with respect to $s=u_1+u_2$ at $s=2$ and multiplying
by a reduction of two predicts a linearized acceleration reduction of
$12\,\mathrm{rad/s^2}$; the actual finite reduction is six. A local slope
is not an exact large intervention. This invented law illustrates the
mathematics; it is not a fitted muscle model.

An algebraic decomposition remains useful when its construction is stated.
Signed acceleration components can cancel, so one may exceed the total.
Near-zero totals make percentage attribution unstable. Report physical units,
closure and the decomposition convention. Reactions depend on the imposed
constraints and other loads; do not silently count the same constraint effect
both inside a solved input response and as a separate independent cause.

### Cut Time, Horizon and Event Are Part of the Experiment

Choosing a cut after seeing the largest difference can exaggerate a result.
Declare cuts, horizons, primary outcomes and event rules before selecting
favorable cases; retain failures and sensitivity results. For exploratory
choices, say how they were selected and test the claim on new cases.

One branch may reach a delivery criterion earlier. Comparing both at the
baseline clock time and comparing each at its own first valid event answer
different questions. Record branches that never reach the event. If the model
stops at contact, do not evaluate an invented post-impact continuation. A
geometric crossing is not a resolved ball collision.

Refinement must check the claimed observable, event localization and input
sampling convention. A one-sample spike deserves investigation, especially
near a command switch; it is not automatically fictitious. A finite jump in
force can be part of the declared model. Conversely, an unresolved spike is
not established as a physical mechanism merely because one solver produced it.
Agreement at two steps alone does not establish an asymptotic convergence order.

### What the Saved Planar Evidence Shows

The pinned technical ensemble uses a rigid single-wrist double pendulum with
a directly prescribed shoulder/wrist torque program. Both joint torques are
set to zero in its comparison branch. Its 96 baseline cases combine eight cut
times, four horizons and three steps. Source states are interpolated from a
registered trace; the record specifies terminal command sampling, including
an endpoint that lands on the torque switch.

An independent arithmetic check of the saved JSON reproduces its complete
case grid and timestep-sensitivity summaries. At the 1 ms reference step,
commanded-minus-zero-torque wrist-force work ranges from about $-30.88$ J to
$66.17$ J. The corresponding terminal clubhead-speed differences are positive:
about $3.42$ and $14.20$ m/s. The minimum work difference occurs at a 0.32 s cut
over 0.12 s; the maximum work difference at a 0.22 s cut over the same horizon.

Within the first comparison, the commanded branch has less wrist-force work
yet a faster clubhead than its zero-torque counterpart. Wrist-moment
work, gravity, initial state and the relationship between total kinetic energy
and head velocity must also be considered. This connects counterfactual design
to the work ledger: identify which transfer channel a reported difference covers.

The saved comparison against a 0.5 ms reference gives a maximum work-difference
change of about 0.0174 J at 1 ms and 0.356 J at 2 ms. Those are sensitivity
results for these cases and this metric, not universal error bounds. The
provider also reports positive zero-torque force-power persistence for selected
cuts; it does not establish phase-independent passive behavior.

Twelve additional rows compare baseline, gravity-disabled and damping-disabled
scenarios at four cuts. Each scenario has its own preceding rollout. These are
whole-model variants, not identical-state partitions of gravity and damping.
Reading the implementation and recomputing saved summary arithmetic does not
constitute a fresh dynamics run or an independent validation of human motion.
Some stored dependency hashes identify older code than the selected provider
revision. These numerical values are archived-output evidence; reproducing them
with that revision remains unverified. The arithmetic check does not repair
that lineage gap.

### Geometry Controls Must Name What Stays Fixed

Write two contact points as $p_1=c+d/2$ and $p_2=c-d/2$, where $c$ is their
midpoint and $d$ their separation vector. For point forces $F_1,F_2$, the
force-generated moment about a reference $O$ is

$$
M_O=(c-O)\times(F_1+F_2)
       +\frac{d}{2}\times(F_1-F_2).
$$

The second term is the differential moment about the midpoint. Its magnitude
satisfies

$$
\lVert M_{\mathrm{diff}}\rVert
\leq \frac{\lVert d\rVert}{2}
       \bigl(\lVert F_1\rVert+\lVert F_2\rVert\bigr).
$$

As separation tends to zero with bounded forces, this differential moment
vanishes. The moment of the resultant about an offset reference need not.
Any independently applied grip moments must also be added. Maintaining a
nonzero differential moment as separation vanishes would require unbounded
forces in this two-point-force representation.

For example, take $O=0$, $c=(0.4,0,0)$ m, $d=(0.1,0,0)$ m,
$F_1=(0,30,0)$ N and $F_2=(0,10,0)$ N. The differential moment is
$1\,\mathrm{N\,m}$ about $+z$; the resultant contributes another
$16\,\mathrm{N\,m}$ about $O$. Collapsing the separation while retaining
these forces removes the differential contribution but leaves
$16\,\mathrm{N\,m}$ about $O$. Adding a direct $2\,\mathrm{N\,m}$ grip
couple would yield $18\,\mathrm{N\,m}$. These are manufactured geometry
checks, not measurements of hand force.

Negating $d$ with $c$ and the forces fixed reverses the differential term, not
the offset-resultant term. Negating every arm about $O$ reverses the entire
force-generated moment about $O$. Neither operation predicts what happens when
new geometry changes contact deformation, force strategy and the subsequent
trajectory. That requires a newly defined, compatible simulation.

### Coordinate Checks Are Different From Physical Reversals

A signed axis component can reverse under a consistent change of coordinates.
For example, a proper 180-degree rotation of the coordinate axes about $x$
changes the coordinates of $M=(0,0,1)\,\mathrm{N\,m}$ to $(0,0,-1)$.
The coordinates of a physical normal $n=(0,0,1)$ change with it, preserving
$n\cdot M=1\,\mathrm{N\,m}$. Transform angular velocity consistently and
$M\cdot\omega$ is also unchanged. A component sign flip alone is not evidence
against the mechanism.

Compare the same physical observable, with a declared normal orientation and
reference point. Transform wrench and velocity together when checking power;
an observer change requires its corresponding velocity and energy accounting.
A planar model cannot supply omitted spatial components simply by relabeling
its output as a complete spatial wrench. Cross-model comparisons must identify
the common observables and the components that each model actually represents.

### What the Spatial Killswitch Tests

At the pinned revision, the reduced spatial study uses finite-mass translating
hand carriages, a rigid club and paired compliant point interfaces. Its
intervention removes the complete grounded spring-damper driver at 0.180 s.
The contact forces continue to arise from relative displacement and velocity;
they are not independently prescribed negative moments.

The saved summary reports a negative swing-normal contact moment after driver
removal, with a minimum near $-0.409\,\mathrm{N\,m}$ and a longest negative
run reported as 37.5 ms. The implementation computes that duration by counting
contiguous negative samples and multiplying by the timestep. It is a sampled
interval statistic, not an exactly located zero-crossing duration. The study's
coincident and reversed-arm controls reuse the achieved forces without advancing
new trajectories: they move both application points to the club reference or
negate both arms about it. They test the wrench mapping under those fixed-force
changes. The saved spatial record also contains an older runner-script hash;
the comparison is cited as archived evidence, not a newly reproduced run.

MuJoCo and Pinocchio independently supply rigid-body operators while sharing
the project contact law and state update. Their agreement is evidence about
that comparison, not independent validation of the shared contact model,
integrator, anatomical arms or human strategy. The carriages are not arms and
the grounded driver is not muscle. Prior external work remains part of the
history even after that driver is removed.

**Model Result:** These declared studies distinguish instantaneous attribution,
forward persistence, whole-model variants and analytical geometry controls.
They establish different, bounded facts rather than one universal explanation.

**Hypothesis:** A proposed transmission mechanism should predict a specific
change under a feasible intervention that removes or alters that mechanism.
The prediction must name the mediator, task, comparison and uncertainty.

**Practical Interpretation:** State what stayed identical, what changed, how
forces were obtained, and how long the altered branch evolved.

### Ablation and Compensation Challenge Different Claims

If an effect survives a correctly implemented removal, the removed mechanism
is not necessary for that effect in that tested setting. If the effect disappears,
that supports dependence in the tested comparison; it does not prove universal
necessity. The removal may also change feasible states, task execution or other
pathways. Identify those changes before attributing the difference narrowly.

Setting a dead zone to zero removes that threshold in the declared law, not
activation delay or every compliant mode. Equalizing two shafts' stiffness
removes that parameter contrast, not flexibility itself. Replacing a flexible
shaft with a rigid constraint changes the state space and requires a declared
state mapping and energy treatment. A valid different model is not necessarily
a negative control that must fail.

If optimization finds a feasible policy without a given actuator that meets
the declared task tolerances, it establishes an alternative in that model and
control family. It does not show the actuator was irrelevant in the baseline,
or that humans possess the same alternative. Failure to find compensation can
reflect controller restrictions or optimization failure rather than physical
impossibility. Report search method, constraints, failures and achieved margins.

Compare internal loads, individual interface powers and sensitivity as well as
the recovered club motion. Equal net wrench or task outcome can conceal very
different bilateral force allocations. Compensation is useful precisely because
it exposes how several mechanisms can meet one visible task at different costs.

### Timing and Human Falsification

To study timing, define whether a command is shifted by clock time or triggered
by a measured state event. Preserve the intended command shape, actuator limits
and input meaning; report which quantities are matched. Different starting
states at different cuts do not create a single identical-state experiment.
A state trigger must use information available at that instant, not a future
impact time known only after the simulated swing finishes.

Rank outcomes explicitly: a command that increases speed can worsen face/path
alignment, peak load or sensitivity. Use declared uncertainty sets and untouched
holdouts; distinguish synthetic parameter draws from new participants. This
connects timing to feasibility and evidence rather than yielding one universal
instruction about when to release.

A human experiment can alter grip spacing, equipment or instructions while
measuring the proposed mediators. Reduced spacing also can change force
magnitude, direction and feedback. The bounded-force identity alone therefore
does not predict a proportional decrease in the measured couple. Use the
observed forces and geometry together, and distinguish total effects of the
manipulation from a narrower hypothesized pathway.

The pinned experimental protocol proposes synchronized measurements, calibration,
residual checks and participant-level holdout. Its saved readiness artifact
qualifies a synthetic dry run; it does not contain human measurements. Protocol
thresholds are declared design choices, not demonstrated measurement accuracy.
The empirical bridge remains model prediction, feasible manipulation,
synchronized observation and a predeclared result that counts against the claim.

### Reader Lab: Build a Branch Manifest

Record the source/model revision, complete state and hash, time/phase, changed
input or law, retained control policies, parameters, contact mode, random inputs,
solver, tolerances, event rule, horizon and primary observables. A retained
feedback policy may generate different future commands as the states diverge;
replaying the same command trace is a different intervention.

First check initial-state equality for an input-only branch. Acceleration,
reaction or power may differ immediately, but need not: a command-only change
behind actuator dynamics may initially leave the mechanical output unchanged.
An unchanged compliant law depending only on the copied state gives identical
initial contact force and interface power even when driver force changes.
For a state intervention, list the deliberately unequal components instead of
requiring every initial difference to vanish. Recheck constraints and stored
energy in either case.

Then plot the declared observable through time, refine timesteps and event
handling, and retain non-reaching or unstable branches. A second implementation
adds evidence only for the components implemented independently. Use the same
frames, references, units and task rules; disclose shared code and model laws.

Compare pointwise, forward and compensated outcomes without selecting only the
most favorable one. A defensible conclusion names the actual intervention:
“At this modeled state, removing this driver changed this reaction,” or
“After that driver was removed, this contact moment persisted over this
horizon.” Calling an endogenous negative couple itself “retained” requires a
different model that explicitly imposes that moment.

## Where the Picture Breaks

The baking analogy captures history dependence, but cannot represent an exact
copied state. Removing damping can change phase and contact forces as well as
energy loss. Precise interventions do not make mechanisms independent or a
model biologically correct.

Randomization and participant holdout strengthen human experiments without
revealing every internal state. Use the model to propose a measurable prediction
and a predeclared observation that would count against it.
